name: collision
description: AABB + SAT collision detection, resolution, messaging; needs physics (a collider's body is a RigidBody/Velocity owner)
postInstallNotes:
## collision installed

Attach `BoxColliderComponent` (AABB) or `ConvexColliderComponent` (SAT) plus the `ColliderTagComponent` marker to entities you want to collide. Both collider types feed the same detection system polymorphically.

`physics` was installed alongside this module: collision resolves a collider's **body** through `RigidBodyComponent`/`VelocityComponent` (`ColliderBody.Resolve`), so the source does not compile without it. Registering `GravitySystem`/`VelocitySystem` in your pipeline stays your call — a trigger-only game can leave both out and still compile.

Pipeline:
1. `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` queries `ColliderTagComponent` entities, computes overlaps, publishes `CollisionMessage` per pair.
2. `TransformCollisionResolutionSystem` resolves every message it receives: it corrects the **body's** position (swept snap, or shortest-exit depenetration when the pair already overlaps) and zeros the velocity component moving into the contact when that body has a `VelocityComponent`. No impulses and no `Mass` — nothing in this module reads `RigidBodyComponent` outside `ColliderBody.Resolve`.
3. `TransformPhysicalCollisionResolutionSystem` is that same resolution narrowed by message TYPE: a subclass whose only override admits a message when `CollisionMessage.Type == CollisionType.Physics`. You set that type in the `CreateCollisionMessageDelegate` you hand to detection — the default is `CollisionType.Generic`, which this system ignores. Register ONE resolution system per entity stack, not both: each handles a given message once, so a `Physics`-tagged contact would otherwise be corrected twice.

Subscribe to `CollisionMessage` in your game systems for trigger logic (pickups, doorways, dialogue zones).

**Premises:** `docs/premises.md`
